note: Proved on points (Grothendieck's own reading X''(Z) ⊂ X'(Z)×X'(Z)): a family of bijections X'_s ≃ X'_t over S'' satisfies the cocycle condition iff the induced relation on X' is an equivalence relation. The scheme version needs descent data of schemes: mathlib has no category of descent data of schemes relative to S' -> S (no pseudofunctor S |-> Sch/S with effectivity results).

On points (in Sets every equivalence relation is universally effective): the quotient X = X'/X'' exists, X'' = X' ×_X X', and X'_s ≃ X_{π s}. The equivalence 'effective iff universally effective' for schemes is not formalised: mathlib has no category of descent data of schemes relative to S' -> S (no pseudofunctor S |-> Sch/S with effectivity results).
The listener's correction (effective and universal equivalence relation) is the content of 16055.

On points: a subset is saturated for X'' iff its inverse images under q1 and q2 coincide. For an open subscheme the condition is set-theoretic because open subschemes are determined by their underlying sets.
Effectivity of descent data of schemes, local on stable opens: mathlib has no category of descent data of schemes relative to S' -> S (no pseudofunctor S |-> Sch/S with effectivity results).
Reading.

Effective descent of relatively affine schemes (quasi-coherent algebras) along fpqc morphisms is not in mathlib (only descent of morphism properties and the effective-epimorphism property); mathlib has no category of descent data of schemes relative to S' -> S (no pseudofunctor S |-> Sch/S with effectivity results).
A faithfully flat quasi-compact morphism is a quotient map; injective (radicial) it is a homeomorphism; the hypotheses are stable under base change.

Proved for X' = S': for g radicial the diagonal is surjective, so the two projections S'' ⇉ S' agree on points and every subset is stable. The general X' (q1 = q2 on points of X'') and the effectivity are not formalised: mathlib has no category of descent data of schemes relative to S' -> S (no pseudofunctor S |-> Sch/S with effectivity results).
Hironaka-type proper smooth non-projective threefold with a non-effective Galois descent datum: no carrier in mathlib (projectivity, ampleness, descent data of schemes).
No relative ampleness of invertible sheaves in mathlib; mathlib has no category of descent data of schemes relative to S' -> S (no pseudofunctor S |-> Sch/S with effectivity results).
No (very) ample invertible sheaves in mathlib. The uniform power L'^n very ample needs S' quasi-compact (EGA II 4.6.11); harmless here since the question is local on S.

Affine case only: for f = Spec(A → B), N a B-module and A → A', N ⊗_B (B ⊗_A A') ≅ N ⊗_A A' (direct image commutes with base change; flatness is needed only for non-affine qcqs f). Descent data on E' not formalised.
Very ample invertible sheaves, projective bundles P(E) of a quasi-coherent sheaf and descent data of schemes are not in mathlib.
Quasi-projective morphisms and descent data of schemes are not in mathlib.
Affine case: Algebra.norm A : B →* A is det of multiplication, multiplicative, sends units to units. The norm of invertible sheaves (torsors under B^*) is not in mathlib.

No ampleness in mathlib. Note: absolute ampleness is not preserved under arbitrary inverse image (pull back O(1) on a point to P^1); the statement is right for inverse image by finite (affine) morphisms, or for relative ampleness under base change, which is the use made here (q1^* M' on X'').
Quasi-projective and projective schemes over a field (ample sheaves) are not in mathlib.

The limit argument (properties of schemes of finite presentation passing to filtered limits of rings) is not in mathlib for general properties; the Nullstellensatz step is (board item 19779, board_19779).
Spreading out isomorphisms of schemes of finite presentation over a filtered colimit of rings is not in mathlib in this form.

Proved on points: if G acts on S' with S' × G → S' ×_S S' surjective (pseudo-torsor), a gluing datum (functional relation over S'') is a descent datum (an equivalence relation) iff it is the orbit relation of an action of G on X' compatible with X' → S'. The group-scheme version needs descent data of schemes.
On points, the constant group is the abstract group Γ: prop_20176 with G = Γ. The scheme version (action of Γ_S = action of Γ) is not restated.
Proved for X = Spec k, Y = A^1 and S' = Spec k' with k'/k Galois: Hom_k = Γ-invariant k'-points, i.e. k = k'^Γ. Full faithfulness in general needs descent of morphisms of schemes.
On points: prop_20176 (a torsor is in particular a pseudo-torsor). Torsors under group schemes are not in mathlib.
Proved: k'/k is faithfully flat of rank [k':k] = |Γ|. The torsor isomorphism k' ⊗_k k' ≅ ∏_Γ k' is not in mathlib and not proved here.
Proved for X = Spec k, Y = A^1: the k-points are the Γ-invariant k'-points (k = k'^Γ). General Galois descent of morphisms of schemes not formalised.
Descent data = actions: on points, prop_20176. Effectivity for quasi-projective X' not formalised (no quasi-projectivity, no descent data of schemes).
Proved: Gal(k'/k) ≅ lim Gal(L/k) over the finite Galois subextensions L. The affine group scheme Γ_k = Spec(colim k^{Γ_i}) and the torsor Spec k' are not formalised.
Γ = lim Γ_i (prop_20102). The k-points of Γ_k = Spec LocallyConstant(Γ, k) and the equivalence descent data = Γ_k-actions are not formalised.
Affine level: the comorphism LocallyConstant(Γ,k) → (Γ → k) of Γ → Γ_k is injective (schematic dominance). That this determines actions is not restated.
Proved for X = Spec k, Y = A^1 and any (possibly infinite) Galois k'/k: k = k'^Γ.
Degree 0 = faithfulness, degree 1 = fullness of X ↦ descent data, for a pseudofunctor F (e.g. relative schemes).
Degree 2 = the functor to descent data is an equivalence (effective descent).
Proved for sheaves (descent of degrees 0, 1 for representable functors) and finite families: the sheaf condition for (S'_i → S) and for ∐ S'_i → S agree. Degree 2 for relative schemes not formalised.

mathlib defines descent data exactly so (isomorphisms u^*X'_i → v^*X'_j for every T and u, v, compatible with pull-back, with hom_self and hom_comp = transitivity), and proves it equivalent to the cocycle form on chosen fibre products.

mathlib's DescentData, indexed by all Y → S factoring through some S'_i, is the category of such cartesian sections in disguise; the formulation via the fibred category over the full subcategory is not stated.

Isomorphisms, open immersions, universally closed and locally of finite type morphisms descend along fpqc morphisms. Immersions (EGA IV 2.7.1) and separatedness (hence properness) are not descended in mathlib.
Gluing of morphisms = representable functors are sheaves (the Zariski and fpqc topologies are subcanonical); morphisms over S into Y are sections of Hom(-, Y) on the induced covering of X.

Degrees 0 and 1 for modules along faithfully flat ring maps are proved in Buffalo.AG.Part03 (descent_exact, thm_35250); effectivity for quasi-coherent modules and affine schemes is not in mathlib; the failure for arbitrary schemes is 18219 (not formalised).
Proved over a field: no rational function f with f^n = X for n ≥ 2 (degree), so λ ↦ λ^n has no section over any non-empty open of G_m. Faithful flatness and the μ_n-relation are not restated.
The diagonal is a section of the base change T ×_S T → T, and {T → S} is an fpqc covering.

mathlib: jointly surjective flat families, quasi-compact in the sense that every affine open of the base is covered by finitely many images of quasi-compact opens; generates the same topology as Grothendieck's definition by finite refinements.

mathlib's reduction: effective descent for the fpqc topology follows from effective descent for the families of the fpqc precoverage. The further reduction to open coverings and single faithfully flat quasi-compact morphisms is not stated.
Derived instances Precoverage.IsStableUnderBaseChange and IsStableUnderComposition.
mathlib's form is stronger: Zariski sheaf plus the sheaf condition for faithfully flat Spec S → Spec R.

Effectivity proved (every epimorphism of sheaves of sets is regular, for a site with sheafification). Stability under base change, distributivity of sums and universality of colimits are not restated.
Existence of quotient sheaves (coequalizers in sheaves). The group structure on G/H and the action of G are not formalised.
The fpqc topology is subcanonical (mathlib instance).
Instance in Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Fpqc.lean: a flat surjective quasi-compact morphism is an effective epimorphism; base changes are again such.
A sieve covers for the canonical topology iff all its pullbacks are effective epimorphic (universally strictly epimorphic).
With the comparisons Zariski ≤ fppf ≤ fpqc.

Proved: a family covers in this sense iff its sieve is covering for ⊥, the coarsest topology (every presheaf is a sheaf). In SGA 4 II 1.1.4 this is the 'topologie grossière', 'discrète' naming the finest one; the word 'discrete' may be the lecturer's (the board says the same).
mathlib generates it from open covers; a family covers iff it has sections locally on an open cover.
Algebraic spaces are not in mathlib.

Proved: representable functors are fpqc sheaves, and for affine target a morphism Spec A → Spec B is determined by its reductions mod I^n when A is I-adically Hausdorff (injectivity of F(A) → lim F(A/I^n)); surjectivity and non-affine targets not formalised; the non-sufficiency is not formalised.
Complex analytic spaces, meromorphic functions and algebraic spaces are not in mathlib.
The 'if' half in schemes: a faithfully flat quasi-compact X → Y is an effective epimorphism (Y is the coequalizer of X ×_Y X ⇉ X). The sheaf-quotient formulation and the converse are not formalised.

Proved for a site with sheafification (e.g. small): sheaves of sets have coequalizers. For the large site of schemes with the fpqc topology the existence of the sheaf quotient involves set-theoretic care, not formalised.
Quotients of schemes by finite locally free equivalence relations (SGA 3 V 4.1) are not in mathlib.
Ample invertible sheaves and quasi-projective schemes are not in mathlib (for X affine the statement is trivial).
Quotients of schemes by finite groups (SGA 1 V 1) are not in mathlib.
Generic quotients by flat equivalence relations (SGA 3 V 8) are not in mathlib.
Only the flatness: over a field every algebra is flat, so the relation defined by H is flat. Quotients G/H of algebraic groups are not in mathlib.
